pipeline.summary: The noise-cancelling-headphones idea was selected as today's strongest reviewed candidate after source and catalogue checks. The remaining order is unchanged: it retains ten viable candidates across engineering, physics, technology, geography and mathematics, so no new ideas were added. Rankings are editorial judgements, not measured demand or a fresh source audit.

ranking.headline: Why aircraft windows have rounded corners
ranking.description: Connect cabin pressure, repeated loading and stress concentrations to the shape of a window opening.
ranking.hook: A small change in shape can change where stress builds up.
ranking.rankReason: Moves ahead of the recent heat-pump revision for topic freshness. It has clear engineering stakes and diagram potential; avoid reducing historical aircraft failures to one cause.
ranking.relevance: Evergreen; do not tie to an accident without verified evidence and a separate scope decision.

ranking.headline: How can cold outdoor air heat your home?
ranking.description: Follow a refrigerant around the cycle to explain how electricity moves heat and why colder weather changes the work required.
ranking.hook: A machine can deliver more heat than the electrical energy it consumes.
ranking.rankReason: Retain the useful Adult-depth revision, but its 13 October release and the recent window-condensation lesson make another thermal topic less urgent. Third place preserves seasonal value behind two different mechanisms.
ranking.relevance: Seasonal relevance to northern-hemisphere heating; evergreen physics. No claim of a verified news trend.

ranking.headline: Why freezing water expands instead of shrinking
ranking.description: Build the explanation from the open structure of ice to its lower density, retaining the existing identity and strengthening its Adult depth.
ranking.hook: The solid takes up more room than the liquid it came from.
ranking.rankReason: Worthwhile existing revision with a clear visual mechanism; lower than the leading heating puzzle to avoid consecutive cold-water topics.
ranking.relevance: Evergreen seasonal puzzle; avoid repeating the separate lake-freezing lesson.

ranking.headline: Why two USB-C cables can charge the same phone differently
ranking.description: Separate the connector shape from negotiated power and cable capabilities, without recommending products or promising model-specific charging speeds.

ranking.headline: What goes wrong when a useful measure becomes the target?
ranking.description: Follow one concrete example from a useful indicator to changed behaviour that makes the indicator less useful.

ranking.headline: Why an unlikely message carries more information
ranking.description: Use surprise to explain Shannon information, separating the technical measure from everyday importance or meaning.

ranking.rankReason: A strong quantitative idea with a compact worked example; it follows the more immediate everyday puzzles and must clearly separate technical information from meaning.
ranking.relevance: Evergreen mathematics and computing; no claim about current communications technology.

ranking.headline: Why Wi-Fi signals behave differently across your home
ranking.description: Compare radio frequencies, obstacles and signal loss to explain why coverage and a connection's advertised capability are different questions.

ranking.relevance: Evergreen radio physics; verify frequency and obstacle comparisons from primary sources when selected, without current product or performance promises.
